system.summary: A numerical substitution (code numbers to letters) proposed by the contributor: 28 independently supported number-to-letter values and one provisional value (60 = Y, later counted by the project as the 29th). Checked by the project on the CEHM images.

prior_solution.where: Two sibling telegrams of 15 and 23 July 1909 carry a contemporary plaintext (CEHM 118140, 118185), used by the contributor as controls. No prior reading of the letter found; issue #245, 4-6 Nov 2026.

conditions.human_role: Alberto Garvía García reported the key and the evidence (issue #245, pull request #308). The project has not seen the CEHM images and has verified none of the values.

solution.what: The contributor aligned eight control sequences from two sibling telegrams of 15 and 23 July 1909 with their plaintexts: seven retained controls give 28 distinct number-to-letter values; an eighth, watermark-affected sequence (AYA) adds 60 = Y, provisional.
Project review of the count in issue #245: the strict count is 28; the images were not reachable from the project's environment, so nothing was compared with them.

Alberto Garvía García sent four CEHM viewer screenshots privately. An AI model read the seven control sequences and the 77 groups of the letter of 15 July on them: all numbers and plaintexts agree with the evidence file; the strict count stays 28, with no number mapped to two letters. With the same table the letter decodes to running Spanish (enemigo, te pronuncies, temor, calma y prudencia, oficios, clubs, Guadalajara) and the 29 July note to LIMANTOUR. Images are private and not in the repository (VERIFICATION.md).

Alberto Garvía García sent a second set of four clearer CEHM screenshots (1920 x 1080, from a computer), again private. An AI model re-read the controls, the letter and the 29 July note on them: all agree with the earlier check; the character after 77 is a typed s, not an e; the 29 July sequence reads 24 46 42 1 31 (CREEL); the group 28 23 24 54 2 is printed as given. The contributor reads that group as n-d-o-s-e (quejándose) with 24 as a slip for an o code, and compares the 48 in situación; the project records it as tentative, because it assumes one error (VERIFICATION.md section 5).

The contributor asked to count 60 = Y. On the clearer image of the telegram of 23 July the sequence 15 60 17 is legible beside the typed 'vaya' (the 58 is under the watermark); 15 and 17 are a in the strict count, so 60 = y. Counted as the 29th strict value, one occurrence like 7 = z and 13 = b (VERIFICATION.md section 6). The contributor's packet still says 28.

Issue #606 (Brice Dudout): the telegram of 19 July 1909, DLI.39.7681.1, carries a pencil gloss 'mañana publicará carta Club iniciador'. Read here on the public CEHM image: 47 56 14 32 19 24 15 37 17 and 24 32 57 14 decrypt with key.tsv to publicara and club. 14 = B and 19 = I, until now fixed by one word of the letter each, are given by a contemporary clear; eleven occurrences of strict values confirmed; nothing contradicted. The public image of the letter of 15 July was fetched too: its 77 groups agree with transcription_7680.txt.

Issue #245, comments of 14 and 21 Nov 2026 (Alberto Garvía García): he asked that the code 79 be shown as a provisional 'Sr. Presidente' instead of '?'. Checked on the public CEHM image of the telegram DLI.39.7677.1 (visor.cehm.org.mx, plain http, 2009 x 2636, not in git), read by an AI model at full size: the cipher lines read 79-1-26-3-41-20-8-11 decla-rado 15-48-31-17-7-16 aclara-ción Ruégote 2-54-47-1-38-3-54 carta mía; the pencilled plain text below the signature begins 'Sr. Presidente enemigo declarado'. The cipher carries the words Sr. Presidente (79), enemigo, aplaza and esperes and leaves declarado, aclaración, Ruégote and carta mía clear, so 79 is the only group where 'Sr. Presidente' stands; it opens the same clause in the letter. The last number of the first line, 11, which was cut off on the phone screenshots, is complete. 79 is a phrase code matched by position in one telegram, read by one AI reader; the owner decided on 21 Nov 2026 that the plain text beside it gives the value (next step).

Decision of the owner (Daniel Bourdeau, 21 Nov 2026) on issue #245: the plain text beside 79 gives its value under the README rule of 19 Nov 2026, so 79 is read as 'Sr. Presidente'. Treated like the other values a contemporary clear gives (26, 41, 20, 11, 14, 19): outside the strict count of 29, marked telegram7677 in key.tsv. The special codes are counted apart (codes_open: 1 open, 77); 84 of 89 and the strict count do not change.

validation.notes: The statistical test needs the Spanish letter model (lang/, es-modern), whose corpus cannot be fetched from this environment (Gutenberg returns 403). The key was instead checked against seven control sequences with plaintext on the CEHM images and by the decoding of the letter into running Spanish (VERIFICATION.md); it is not independent of the reading.

outcome.notes: Key proposed by Alberto Garvía García (28 strict values in his count; the project counts 60 = Y too, 29), checked against the CEHM images by an AI reader on 6 Nov 2026 (VERIFICATION.md). Read in part: the letter of 15 July (segment C tentative) and the names in the note of 29 July.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Counted by hand from key.tsv and the decryption files: letter of 15 July 75 of 75 alphabetic groups read as letters of words (two of them, 24 in quejándose and 48 in situación, only by assuming a one-number slip; the special codes are counted apart in codes_open: 79 is read as "Sr. Presidente" from the plain text of the 15 July telegram, 77 is not read) and the note of 29 July 9 of 14 (LIMANTOUR; the second name, 5 groups, is tentative and not counted): 84 of 89 = 94.4%. The control telegrams are not counted.

texts.label: López Portillo y Rojas to Bernardo Reyes, Mexico, 15 July 1909 (CEHM DLI.39.7680.2)
texts.summary: A friend of General Reyes, then governor of Nuevo León, warns him in July 1909 that the President speaks of him as an enemy and urges him not to declare himself at once, to keep calm and be prudent and to look after his health; other clubs of Guadalajara will write; he sends a pleading message the same day; the one complaint is quejándose (tentative).

reading_review.note: Read the decryption as Spanish sentences: enemigo, quejándose (24 as a slip for an o code, tentative), te pronuncies, temor, situación, calma, prudencia, oficios, clubs, Guadalajara form coherent clauses; two codes and one name are open.

texts.label: López Portillo y Rojas to Reyes, 29 July 1909: the cipher sequences (CEHM DLI.39.7712.1)
texts.summary: A short note of 29 July: there is a rupture between Limantour and (probably) Creel; the typed line asks Reyes to put his worries aside and read the reply carefully.

reading_review.note: Only two names are ciphered; LIMANTOUR is secure, the second name is tentative.

texts.label: The two control telegrams of 15 and 23 July 1909 (numbers and plain words)

texts.summary: Short telegrams: the President is a declared enemy and postpones an explanation; Dr. Gómez must go; graves matters; clubs to be told to hold their replies.
